query: For refractory high-entropy alloys intended as energetic structural materials, what single testable hypothesis identifies an intervention that could improve ductility and uniform deformability without sacrificing high strength or impact-induced energy release? State the proposed intervention, its hypothesized mechanism, the improvement expected relative to the untreated baseline, the conditions under which it should hold, the prior evidence supporting it, and a decisive experiment that could falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Refining the grain size of a refractory high‐entropy alloy via severe plastic deformation to submicron levels will enhance room‐temperature ductility and uniform plastic deformability without sacrificing its high strength or impact‐induced energy release.
generation.material_initial_state: As‐cast WMoNbTi refractory high‐entropy alloy with average grain size ~50 µm, yield strength ~1.0 GPa, uniform elongation ~2%, and ignition threshold velocity ~450 m/s.
generation.intervention: High‐pressure torsion processing to achieve average grain size <500 nm.
generation.conditions: Room‐temperature tensile testing at a nominal strain rate of 10^−3 s^−1; impact‐induced ignition testing at velocities between 400 m/s and 500 m/s.
generation.structural_mediator: Increased grain‐boundary density from submicron grains.
generation.mechanism: Hall–Petch strengthening raises yield stress while the high density of grain boundaries impedes strain localization, promoting more homogeneous dislocation activity and extended uniform deformation. Under dynamic loading, the fine‐grained structure partitions deformation into multiple micro‐shear bands that still generate sufficient adiabatic heating for ignition.
generation.predicted_outcome: Yield strength ≥1.2 GPa; uniform elongation ≥10%; ignition threshold velocity within ±10% of 450 m/s.
generation.baseline: Yield strength ~1.0 GPa; uniform elongation ~2%; ignition threshold ~450 m/s in as‐cast coarse‐grained state.
generation.boundary: Applies for refined grain sizes in the range 0.1–1 µm at strain rates from 10^−3 to 10^3 s^−1 and at room temperature.
generation.uncertainty: Moderate uncertainty (~±10%) in the absolute ignition‐threshold change.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two RHEA batches: (1) as‐cast coarse‐grained (~50 µm) and (2) HPT‐processed fine‐grained (<500 nm). Perform quasi‐static tensile tests and split‐Hopkinson pressure bar impact‐ignition tests.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: Hypothesis is falsified if fine‐grained samples do not exhibit at least a 5 % absolute increase in uniform elongation, or if yield strength decreases by more than 10 %, or if ignition threshold velocity shifts by more than 10 % relative to the as‐cast baseline.
